instruction:
Investigate a bug in the Go repository checked out at /gin. The user reports: 'There is a bug in `errors.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestErrorUnwrap` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour.'

Your job in THIS step is ONLY investigation and reporting. Do NOT edit any files.

Steps:
1. Run `cd /gin && ls -la` and `git log --oneline -5` and `git status` to understand the repo (which Go project is it, what version).
2. Print the full contents of the file named `errors.go` (find it with `find /gin -name errors.go`).
3. Print all files in the same package/directory as errors.go.
4. Search the repo for any usage of the types/functions defined in errors.go (e.g. `grep -rn "ErrorType\|Unwrap\|Errors" /gin --include=*.go`).
5. Search for any existing tests referencing errors (e.g. `grep -rn "Error" /gin --include=*_test.go`).
6. Report: the exact full text of errors.go, the package name, the module path from go.mod, all usages found, and your analysis of what the bug is and what `TestErrorUnwrap` would expect. A test named TestErrorUnwrap for an error type typically checks that `errors.Unwrap(err)` or `err.Unwrap()` returns the wrapped error, or that `errors.Is`/`errors.As` works. Explain precisely what the current code does and what it should do to satisfy standard Go error-unwrapping semantics.

Report back with concrete file paths, line numbers, and exact code snippets.

You are working in the Go repository checked out at /gin (the gin web framework). The user reports a bug: 'There is a bug in `tree.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour.'

IMPORTANT COORDINATION NOTE: another agent is concurrently editing /gin/tree.go to fix a DIFFERENT bug (route params). So: (a) make only SURGICAL, minimal edits with `edit_file` using unique surrounding context; never rewrite or reformat the whole file; (b) immediately before editing, re-read the relevant region of tree.go with `sed -n 'START,ENDp' /gin/tree.go` to get current line content, and after editing run `cd /gin && git diff tree.go` to confirm your change is present and that you did not clobber the other agent's change (if you see other unrelated changes in the diff, that's the other agent — leave them alone).

Your job: investigate, fix, and verify.

Steps:
1. `cd /gin && git status && cat go.mod`.
2. BEFORE editing, record the test baseline: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/before_tests_ci.txt | tail -60`. Note any already-failing tests.
3. Print tree.go with line numbers: `cat -n /gin/tree.go`.
4. Print the test files that exercise the tree: `cat -n /gin/tree_test.go` (and grep for findCaseInsensitivePath usages: `grep -rn "findCaseInsensitivePath\|FindCaseInsensitivePath\|CaseInsensitive" /gin --include=*.go`).
5. Analyze the function `findCaseInsensitivePath` (and its helper `findCaseInsensitivePathRec`) in tree.go. A test named TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard would set up a tree with several children plus a wildcard/param node and call findCaseInsensitivePath with a lowercase (or differently-cased) path, expecting the correct resolved path and `found=true`. Look for a logic bug: e.g. wrong handling of the wildcard/param child, incorrect `ciPath` length, wrong index arithmetic, missing handling of the `*` wildcard case, off-by-one, or a case where multiple children exist and the loop mishandles them. Compare against the documented behavior in the repo (comments in tree.go, README/docs, and how gin.go/routergroup.go use it).
6. Apply a minimal, surgical fix. Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT add new features.
7. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`. NO previously-passing test may fail. If your change breaks a pre-existing passing test, revert it (or refine) — breaking a pre-existing green test is unacceptable.
8. Write a TEMPORARY test file in /gin (e.g. /gin/tmp_ci_test.go) that reproduces the expected behavior of findCaseInsensitivePath with multiple children and a wildcard, run `go test -run TmpCI ./...`, then DELETE the temp file and confirm with `git status` that only tree.go (and possibly other files edited by the other agent) are modified.

Report back: exact bug (line numbers, code before/after), `git diff tree.go`, before/after test results, and confirmation that no pre-existing passing test now fails. If no clear repository-evident bug is found, report findings and make NO speculative edits.

You are working in the Go repository checked out at /gin (github.com/gin-gonic/gin v1.8.1). The user reports a bug: 'There is a bug in `context.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour.'

IMPORTANT COORDINATION NOTE: other agents are concurrently editing /gin/context.go (a content-negotiation bug), /gin/tree.go and /gin/response_writer.go. Make only SURGICAL, minimal edits with `edit_file` using unique surrounding context; never rewrite the whole file. Immediately before editing, re-read the region with `sed -n 'START,ENDp' /gin/context.go`. After editing run `cd /gin && git diff context.go` and confirm your change is present (other agents' changes may also appear — leave them alone).

YOUR TASK: investigate, fix, and verify.

Steps:
1. `cd /gin && git status && git diff --stat`.
2. BEFORE editing, record the baseline: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/before_tests_esc.txt | tail -40`.
3. Find the attachment code: `grep -n "Attachment\|Content-Disposition\|filename" /gin/context.go` and print the region with line numbers.
4. Print the existing tests: `grep -rn "Attachment" /gin --include=*_test.go` and print those test functions in full.
5. Analyze `func (c *Context) Attachment(filename string, file io.Reader)` (or similar). A test named TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment would call `c.Attachment("file name.txt", ...)` or a filename containing special characters (spaces, quotes, non-ASCII) and check that the `Content-Disposition` header is properly escaped/quoted (e.g. `attachment; filename="file name.txt"`). Look for a bug: e.g. missing quoting, missing escaping of `"` and `\`, wrong use of `url.PathEscape` vs quoting, or a filename parameter being ignored. The docstring/comments in context.go and any repo docs are the contract.
6. Apply a minimal, surgical fix. Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT add features.
7. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. NO previously-passing test may fail. If your change breaks a pre-existing passing test, revert or refine it.
8. Write a TEMPORARY test file /gin/tmp_attach_test.go reproducing the expected behavior, run `go test -run TmpAttach ./...`, then DELETE it and confirm `git status` shows no untracked file from you.

Report back: exact bug (line numbers, code before/after), `git diff context.go` (only your hunk), before/after test results, and confirmation no pre-existing passing test now fails. If no clear repository-evident bug is found, report findings and make NO speculative edits.

You are working in the Go repository checked out at /gin (the gin web framework). The user reports a bug: 'There is a bug in `context.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestContextNegotiationFormat2` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour.'

IMPORTANT COORDINATION NOTE: other agents are concurrently editing /gin/tree.go and /gin/response_writer.go. Do NOT touch those files. Make only SURGICAL, minimal edits to /gin/context.go with `edit_file` using unique surrounding context; never rewrite the whole file. Immediately before editing, re-read the region with `sed -n 'START,ENDp' /gin/context.go`. After editing, run `cd /gin && git diff context.go` to confirm.

Your job: investigate, fix, and verify.

Steps:
1. `cd /gin && git status && cat go.mod`.
2. BEFORE editing, record the test baseline: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/before_tests_ctx.txt | tail -60`.
3. Find the content-negotiation code: `grep -n "Negotiate\|negotiation\|Accept\|MIME\|ContentType" /gin/context.go | head -60` then print the relevant region with line numbers (`sed -n '1,80p'` and the Negotiate function region).
4. Print the existing tests for negotiation: `grep -rn "Negotiate" /gin --include=*_test.go` and print the relevant test functions in full.
5. Analyze `func (c *Context) Negotiate(code int, config Negotiate)`. A test named TestContextNegotiationFormat2 would test `c.NegotiateFormat(offered ...string) string` or `Negotiate` with an Accept header, expecting the best matching format. Look for a bug in the matching logic: e.g. wrong handling of `*/*`, `application/*`, `q=` quality values, case-insensitivity, `+json` suffix handling, or the returned value when nothing matches. Compare with the documented behavior in the repo (docstrings/comments in context.go, README, docs, and any vendored/related code) — the docstring is the contract.
6. Apply a minimal, surgical fix. Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT add new features.
7. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`. NO previously-passing test may fail. If your change breaks a pre-existing passing test, revert or refine it.
8. Write a TEMPORARY test file in /gin (e.g. /gin/tmp_neg_test.go) reproducing the expected behavior, run `go test -run TmpNeg ./...`, then DELETE the temp file and confirm with `git status` that only context.go is modified by you.

Report back: exact bug (line numbers, code before/after), `git diff context.go`, before/after test results, and confirmation no pre-existing passing test now fails. If no clear repository-evident bug is found, report findings and make NO speculative edits.

Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour.'

2. BEFORE making any edits, run the full test suite and record results: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/before_tests_tree.txt | tail -60`.
3. Print `tree.go` with line numbers: `cat -n /gin/tree.go` (it may be long; that's fine).
4. Print `tree_test.go` and any other test files exercising the router/tree.
5. Understand the bug. A test named TestRouteParamsNotEmpty likely registers routes with params like `/user/:name` and checks that `c.Params` (route params) are not empty / are correctly parsed, or that a param route conflicts. Look for a divergence from behavior documented in the repo (comments/docstrings in tree.go, README, docs in the repo, gin.go, routergroup.go).
6. Apply a minimal fix in /gin/tree.go. Do not change any test file. Do not add features.
7. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`. Compare with the before results: NO previously-passing test may now fail.
8. Optionally write a temporary test file inside /gin to reproduce the expected behavior, run it, then DELETE it so the repo is unchanged except tree.go. Verify with `git status` that only tree.go is modified.

You are working in the Go repository at /gin (github.com/gin-gonic/gin). Other agents have been applying bug fixes to /gin/errors.go, /gin/tree.go, /gin/response_writer.go and /gin/context.go. Your job is a READ-ONLY audit + verification (do NOT edit any file except as noted in step 5).

Steps:
1. `cd /gin && git status --short && git diff --stat`.
2. Dump the FULL current `git diff` (`cd /gin && git diff`) and report it verbatim in your final report.
3. Print the full current text of `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` in /gin/tree.go (`awk '/func \(n \*node\) findCaseInsensitivePathRec/,/^}/' /gin/tree.go | cat -n`) and also `sed -n '780,880p' /gin/tree.go`.
4. Run `cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./... ; go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40` and report the full output.
5. Check for leftover temporary test files: `ls /gin/*tmp* /gin/zz_* 2>/dev/null; git status --short`. If any untracked temp test file exists (names containing 'tmp' or 'zz_'), DELETE it (`rm -f`) so the repo contains only the source fixes. Do not delete any file that is tracked by git.
6. Report: the full git diff, the findCaseInsensitivePathRec source, the test results, and the list of files you deleted (if any).

You are working in the Go repository checked out at /gin (this is the gin web framework). The user reports a bug: 'There is a bug in `response_writer.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestResponseWriterStatusCode` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour.'

Your job: investigate, fix the bug, and verify. Work only inside /gin.

Steps:
1. `cd /gin && git status && git log --oneline -3 && cat go.mod` (note the module path).
2. BEFORE making any edits, run the full pre-existing test suite and record the result: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -50`. Save the list of any already-failing tests to /tmp/before_tests.txt (e.g. `go test ./... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/before_tests.txt`).
3. Print the full contents of `response_writer.go` with line numbers (`cat -n /gin/response_writer.go`).
4. Print the full contents of `response_writer_test.go` if it exists, and any other test file that tests response writer.
5. Search for all usages of the ResponseWriter methods: `grep -rn "\.Status()\|\.Size()\|\.Written()\|WriteHeaderNow\|\.Status(" /gin --include=*.go`.
6. Determine the bug. A test named TestResponseWriterStatusCode would check that `c.Writer.Status()` returns the HTTP status code that was set (e.g. after `c.Status(200)` / `c.Writer.WriteHeader(404)` / default 200 after writing a body). Look for a divergence from expected behavior that is evident from the repository itself (docstrings/comments in the file, README, other code that relies on the behavior). Do NOT invent new features; fix only the bug.
7. Apply a minimal fix with `edit_file` (or python/sed) in /gin/response_writer.go. Do not modify any *_test.go file.
8. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./... 2>&1 | head -20 && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -50`. Compare with /tmp/before_tests.txt: NO previously-passing test may now fail. If your change breaks a pre-existing passing test, revert or adjust the fix so it does not.
9. Also write a small throwaway test in /tmp (NOT in the repo) or use a temporary file outside the repo to check the expected behavior, e.g. a small Go program in /tmp that imports github.com/gin-gonic/gin... (that may be hard due to module paths; instead you may create a temporary test file in /gin, run it, then DELETE it so the repo is unchanged except response_writer.go).

Report back: the exact bug found (file, line numbers, code before/after), the diff of your change (`cd /gin && git diff`), the before/after test suite results, and confirmation that no pre-existing passing test now fails. If you could not find a clear repository-evident bug, report your findings and DO NOT make speculative edits.
